title: Cross-language lockfile consolidation, transitive dep pruning, and stable compatibility gates
creator: Emma Chen
description: Rationalize and shrink the transitive dependency surface across Python, JavaScript, and Go client libraries; consolidate lockfiles and introduce CI compatibility gates to prevent runaway transitive upgrades. As part of this work we will remove legacy API flags/fields from client payload wrappers, provide codemods and migration docs, and validate that optimized packaging reduces install footprint and cold-start times for serverless/edge use cases.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Single source-of-truth dependency policy documented and approved by Platform Security and SDK leads
A2: Consolidated lock strategy implemented: pip-compile generated requirements.txt for Python, npm-shrinkwrap / package-lock policy for JS, and go.sum stabilization for Go
A3: CI compatibility gates added that fail builds when a transitive dependency update introduces a semver-major or is flagged by vuln scans
A4: Legacy client fields (legacy_response_wrapper, preserve_compat_mode, legacy_tracing_flags) removed from public SDK surface or behind a documented deprecation flag with migration path
A5: Integration tests across example apps (serverless, dedicated, private) pass within baseline latency and binary size regressions <= 5%
A6: Migration codemods and CHANGELOG entries published plus PRs merged to python-sdk, js-client, go-client repos
tasks: T1: Audit current transitive dependency graph across all SDK repos and produce delta spreadsheet (owner: Rafael)
T2: Propose consolidated lockfile policy and get sign-off from Security and Developer Experience
T3: Implement pip-compile pipeline and update Python release workflow
T4: Lock npm install matrix and add shrinkwrap verification step to JS CI
T5: Pin go module versions and add go mod vendor verification in CI for reproducible builds
T6: Add CI rule to run `dep-gate` that compares lockfile diffs and blocks unreviewed transitive major bumps
T7: Write codemod for removing legacy_response_wrapper + tests and integration examples
T8: Run bundle-size and install-time benchmarks and publish results to the dashboard
T9: Publish migration guide and deprecation cadence in SDK docs
T10: Coordinate staged rollout and feature-flagged consumer-facing deprecation notice

notes: Implementation approach favors conservative pinning and human review for any transitive major version changes that affect native builds.
Plan aims to reduce accidental vulnerability churn and improve reproducible releases for on-prem and Dedicated customers who rely on offline installs.
If we see >5% regressions in cold-start time for serverless examples after dependency changes, we will rollback dependent changes and open a perf investigation ticket.
